How to unclog a toilet if you don't have a plunger

Great for when a client clogs the only toilet at your workplace and you have no plunger!

A few additional tips:

If the toilet is overflowing-open the tank, lift the flapper to stop water coming in and then turn off the water supply near the bottom of the toilet.

Detailed instructions here- http://lentheplumber.com/plumbing/stop-overflowing-toilet/

The water level should go down during the 20 min. or so that you let the soap sit in the bowl.

Turn the water back on when you are ready to try to flush the clog away.

If you still have a clog after trying this method then add a little more soap and hot water and let it sit for another 30 minutes.

Then fill a container (a large cup, bucket, whatever) with hot water. You want at least 2 or 3 cups of water. Very forcefully pour this water into the bowl. It should immediately "flush" the clog away.
Use caustic soda and boiling water, don't put your hand in the water...
I wouldn't use boiling water. Hot is ok, but if it's too hot you could crack the porcelain bowl!
Buy a fucking plunger. Or preferably an auger. The auger is more expensive, but itll clean that toilet like nothing else(short of pulling and reseating).

Sometimes you find yourself without a plunger. We didn't have one at work when a client decided to drop a massive toilet buster. We did have one but it apparently walked out of the building at some point. (Who steals plungers?!) No one really knows what happened to it? There was no one available to go buy one at that time and it was the only toilet. I used this method to get it unclogged. I was also able to do this when I clogged the toilet immediately after moving in to my new house (but before buying a new plunger). Kept me from having to live with a clogged toilet overnight.

So, yeah, a plunger is always the best solution, but if you find yourself without one this can work.
